Instagram Outreach: A Practical Guide to Getting Clients

Instagram outreach is the practice of starting relevant conversations with potential clients or partners on Instagram. A good first DM gives the recipient a clear reason to respond, even if they have never heard of you. Start with one audience, one offer and one next step so you can see what gets a response.

Get started with ColdNerd

1. Define who to contact and why now

Write your audience as a sentence your team could use to make a decision. A video editing agency might look for Pilates studio owners who have announced an upcoming class launch and already publish short instructor demos. The audience is the studio owner. The timing signal is the launch. The offer is turning one existing clip into a short launch Reel.

2. Build a shortlist with evidence

Look at public business profiles, industry directories, event speaker lists, local business pages and partnerships. Record the profile URL, decision maker or business contact, the public signal you noticed, and the date you checked it. Recent activity can tell you where to look, while follower count alone tells you little about budget or intent.

Before writing, confirm that the business fits your offer, that your observation is accurate, and that you can explain the connection in one sentence. Skip accounts with no clear fit, people who have declined, and prospects already in a conversation with your team.

Ready to build a list? Read the Instagram prospecting guide.

3. Write a first DM that earns a reply

Use three parts: a verified observation, a connection to a specific outcome, and a small question. You can offer something easy to assess, such as two ideas or a short outline. Save a calendar link, portfolio reel or long pitch for when the person asks for more.

Template for a freelancer or agency

Hey [name], saw that [public launch or announcement]. I edit short videos for [relevant niche], and your [existing asset] gave me an idea for [specific outcome]. Want me to send two quick concepts here?

Template for a local B2B service

Hi [name], congrats on opening [location]. I work with [type of business] on [specific outcome]. I noticed [verified public detail] and had one idea for [opportunity]. Would a short note here be useful?

Template for a creator partnership

Hey [name], your post on [specific topic] made me think of a short [format] we could make together for [shared audience]. I can handle [your contribution]. Want the two-sentence outline?

Read the DM aloud. If the opening would work on 20 unrelated accounts, make it more specific. If you name a problem you cannot verify, present it as a question. If you offer an example, prepare it before anyone replies.

4. Follow up only when you have something to add

If someone hasn't replied and a follow-up is appropriate, wait a few business days and send one useful extra. For the Pilates studio, you could share an example hook: “One idea for the launch Reel: open with three seconds of the class in motion, then put the date on screen before the first instruction.”

A silent thread can end there. Close it in your tracker instead of chasing the person across channels. If someone declines or asks you to stop, update your shared contact list so another teammate doesn't message them again.

5. Turn interest into the right next step

If they say “send it,” share what you promised in the DM. Then ask one question that helps you understand fit, such as “Is the goal trial bookings, or awareness for the new class?” Once you understand the goal, suggest a short call only if it would help both sides make a decision.

A reply you can adapt

Here are the two hooks I had in mind. The first leads with the class experience. The second leads with the timetable. Which feels closer to your launch? If you want help choosing footage, I can walk through it with you in 15 minutes.

Keep one owner on the thread. Record what you promised, your next action and its date. Use clear statuses such as ready, contacted, replied, interested, call booked and closed so a teammate can pick up where you left off.

6. Measure outcomes by audience and offer

Compare batches from the week you first contacted each prospect. Pick a consistent reply window, such as seven days, and count each person once. Use a spreadsheet with columns for audience segment, offer, first-contact date, reply status, positive reply, call booked and outcome. Mark “positive” only when there is actual interest or a request for more information.

The illustration uses example data. Reply rate is 8 ÷ 40 = 20%. Positive reply rate is 4 ÷ 40 = 10%. Booked call rate is 2 ÷ 40 = 5%. In your records, separate interested replies from declines and log calls held separately from calls booked.

Few replies? Recheck the audience and the specificity of the opening. Plenty of replies but little interest? Test whether the offer solves a problem that matters now. Interested replies with few bookings? Review what happens after they ask for more. Change one variable at a time and treat small samples as directional.

Instagram outreach FAQs

Is Instagram outreach useful for B2B?

It's a fit when buyers actively use business profiles and publicly share useful context. If buyers rarely check their DMs, choose the contact channel they make available.

How many DMs should I send per day?

There's no universal safe number. Your starting point should be how many prospects you can research and respond to thoughtfully. Respect Instagram's rules and stop if the platform restricts an action.
